o1.biggest_strength: It spots the in-app checkout issue as a ship-now bug, sizes the upside in money, and then gives a sensible ranked test plan tied back to the actual evidence in the brief.
o1.biggest_mistake: It says Test 1 main metric is orders per session on all devices but gives a 0.70% baseline that blends devices loosely, and the note about running paired tests on 'separate splits' is a bit hand-wavy for experiment design.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the measurement math and experiment setup, make the baselines fully explicit by device after the bug fix, and be sharper about what ships without testing versus what truly needs a test.

o2.biggest_strength: It leads exactly where I would want: fix the in-app browser checkout bug first, quantify the profit at stake, and then rank five tests around the biggest known customer questions.
o2.biggest_mistake: It leaves out moving the 100-night trial and reviews higher as explicit tests or stronger ship recommendations, and some projected rupee impacts from add-to-cart lifts rely on rough assumptions that are not fully explained.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep the same priority order but add a crisper ship-now list around trial, reviews and delivery visibility, and make the payoff estimates for the add-to-cart tests more rigorous and less back-of-envelope.

reason: Both are strong and I would use either with edits, but 2 is a touch better on owner judgment: cleaner prioritisation, stronger call on the bug, and more realistic framing of what the tests can and cannot detect.
